core_obligations: Fix a morphism Y -> X from a scheme whose image factors through Z, and pull it back along X' -> X (proof lines 8248-8251).
Show that the pulled back morphism Y x_X X' -> X' factors through Z' (proof lines 8250-8252).
Record that the infinitesimal neighbourhoods satisfy Z'_n = X' x_X Z_n for all n >= 1 (proof lines 8252-8254).
Conclude the cartesian square of functors from the colimit formulas X^_Z = colim Z_n and (X')^_{Z'} = colim Z'_n (proof lines 8254-8256).
Read off that (X')^_{Z'} -> X^_Z is representable by algebraic spaces as the base change of the morphism of sheaves involved (statement lines 8245-8246).
proof_roadmap: Test-object reduction to a scheme Y over X factoring through Z (proof lines 8248-8251).
Pull back and identify the factorisation through Z' (proof lines 8250-8252).
Compare infinitesimal neighbourhoods and pass to the colimit presentation (proof lines 8252-8256).
difficulty_reason: The statement is that for a morphism f : X' -> X of algebraic spaces over S and a closed subspace Z of X with inverse image Z', the square formed by the completions (X')^_{Z'}, X^_Z and the morphisms to X' and X is cartesian, and in particular the induced map (X')^_{Z'} -> X^_Z is representable by algebraic spaces (statement lines 8232-8246). The proof derives the cartesian square from the colimit presentation of both completions: a morphism Y -> X from a scheme that factors through Z is taken, the fibre product Y x_X X' is shown to factor through Z', the equality of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods Z'_n = X' x_X Z_n is recorded for all n, and the two colimit formulas X^_Z = colim Z_n and (X')^_{Z'} = colim Z'_n then give the claim (proof lines 8248-8257). The level is H2: the card is short, but the reader has to run the colimit presentation through a scheme-valued test object and observe that the infinitesimal neighbourhoods are pulled back exactly.
